A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CASR and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, and references. All ten pages of each were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CASR evaluations on DIV8K, RealSR, and CelebA-HQ, plus component, loss, and superpixel-size ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds an ablation isolating global semantic context within SARM.

M1.justification: Equation (4) changes the stated reconstruction-loss term from L1 to L2, resolving its inconsistency with Figure 3, which already displayed L2 in v1. This is a limited correction to the specified objective; the PDFs do not establish changed training execution. The cyclic architecture remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on DF2K and evaluate the same synthetic, real-world, and face tasks using DIV8K, RealSR, and CelebA-HQ. The evaluated magnification scenarios are retained; the new ablation introduces no additional data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain LINF, BFSR, IDM, Kim, LIIF+Diff, and CiaoSR+Diff; Table 3 retains IDM and Kim. Figures 6–7 change LINF-LP labels to BFSR while retaining the images, consistent with the existing tables and discussion.

E3.justification: New Table 5 introduces a controlled comparison with and without global-semantic conditioning in SARM at ×18 using ×4 ×3 ×1.5 cascading. Existing dataset selections, metrics, training budgets, patch sizes, and overlap settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.5.2 and new Table 5 isolate the contribution of global-semantic cross-attention beyond SARM's self-attention. Existing component, loss, and superpixel-size ablations remain; the loss ablation gains explanatory prose rather than new measurements.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2 retains point-estimate reporting for both existing results and the new ablation.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports the variant without global semantics: LPIPS 0.469, MUSIQ 49.10, NIQE 6.30, and PI 5.49. Its full-model row repeats 0.450, 51.44, 6.01, and 5.24. All numerical entries in the preexisting tables and the underlying qualitative images are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (4) locally revises the mathematical definition of the reconstruction objective by replacing L1 with L2. Scale factorization, superpixel averaging, correlation equations, and the remaining loss formulas are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that a reusable cyclic model stabilizes arbitrary-scale super-resolution through structural alignment and self-similarity refinement, achieving superior extreme-scale reconstruction. Renaming SDAM to SSAM and refining the correlation terminology do not change the main contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.5.2 newly interprets global semantic conditioning as complementary to inter-patch self-attention. Section 4.5.3 adds loss-specific interpretations of existing measurements. The previously discussed tradeoff between artifact suppression and detail loss from larger superpixels remains.

D1.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4.3 newly specify bottleneck-feature caching, attention over cached features, independent patch decoding, MultiDiffusion merging, and RAM-generated prompts at each scale. These improve implementation documentation without establishing that these procedures were newly introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Adversarial Diffusion Distillation for SD-Turbo and Recognize Anything for RAM. It also explicitly attributes patch merging to the already-cited MultiDiffusion. The related-work discussion and broader novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 renames SDAM to SSAM, clarifies SARM explanations, condenses results discussions, adds ablation subsection headings and acknowledgments, and edits author and affiliation information. The overall narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the global-context ablation table, adjusts Figure 3's layout, corrects baseline labels in Figures 6–7, and rearranges or resizes existing displays. The previous loss and superpixel-size tables become Tables 6 and 7; their content is retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's whole-module ablation, v2's new Table 5 provides more specific evidence for global semantic conditioning within SARM. Added implementation details and the loss-equation correction improve reproducibility and consistency. These are localized gains: existing benchmark results remain unchanged, and Figure 3 still retains the old SDAM label despite the textual rename.
